title: Independence from Sums Omitting a Coordinate
statement: Let $(\Omega,\mu)$ be a probability space, let $n$ be a natural number, and let $X_j:\Omega\to\bbr$ for $j\in\{0,\ldots,n-1\}$ be mutually independent and almost everywhere measurable. Let $F$ and $G$ be real coefficient families on subsets of the coordinate set, let $s$ be a subset of that set, and let $i$ be a coordinate with $i\notin s$. Then $X_i$ is independent of the pair consisting of $\sum_{T\subseteq s}F(T)\prod_{j\in T}X_j$ and $\sum_{T\subseteq s}G(T)\prod_{j\in T}X_j$.
hypotheses_covered: $F,G$ are real coefficient families on subsets of the coordinate set
$s$ is a subset of the coordinate set
replaced: Let $(X_j)_{j\in[n]}$ be mutually independent, almost everywhere measurable real functions on a measure space $(\Omega,\mu)$, let $s\subseteq[n]$ and $i\notin s$, and let $F,G$ be real coefficient families on subsets of $[n]$. Then $X_i$ is independent of the pair $(\sum_{T\subseteq s}F(T)\prod_{j\in T}X_j,\sum_{T\subseteq s}G(T)\prod_{j\in T}X_j)$.
